record.original_question: Consider the rational difference equations x_{n+k} = (A0 + A1 x_n + ... + Ak x_{n+k-1})/(B0 + B1 x_n + ... + Bk x_{n+k-1}) with positive-coefficient assumptions as stated in the paper. Are there periodic equations of this form that are not equivalent to the five known examples x_{n+1}=x_n, x_{n+1}=1/x_n, x_{n+2}=x_{n+1}/x_n, x_{n+2}=(1+x_{n+1})/x_n, and x_{n+3}=(1+x_{n+1}+x_{n+2})/x_n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider rational difference equations of the form
   x_{n+k} = (A_0 + A_1 x_n + A_2 x_{n+1} + ... + A_k x_{n+k-1}) / (B_0 + B_1 x_n + B_2 x_{n+1} + ... + B_k x_{n+k-1}),
where k ≥ 1 is an integer and the coefficients A_0,...,A_k, B_0,...,B_k are nonnegative real numbers, with the positivity conditions ensuring that, for any positive initial conditions x_0, x_1, ..., x_{k-1} > 0, the recurrence is well-defined and produces a sequence of positive real numbers. Such an equation is called globally periodic if there exists a positive integer p such that x_{n+p} = x_n for all n ≥ 0 and for every choice of positive initial conditions.

Two equations of this form are called equivalent if one can be transformed into the other by a change of variables of the form y_n = α x_{n+s}^{±1} (with α > 0 and s ∈ ℤ), or more generally by Möbius-type transformations preserving the form of the family.

The following five equations are globally periodic examples within this family:
   (i)   x_{n+1} = x_n              (period 1),
   (ii)  x_{n+1} = 1/x_n            (period 2),
   (iii) x_{n+2} = x_{n+1}/x_n      (period 6),
   (iv)  x_{n+2} = (1 + x_{n+1})/x_n   (period 5),
   (v)   x_{n+3} = (1 + x_{n+1} + x_{n+2})/x_n   (period 8).

Question: Does there exist a globally periodic rational difference equation of the above form that is not equivalent to any of the five equations (i)–(v)?
artifact.status_search_result: The global periodicity problem for rational difference equations is a long-standing open problem. Surveys (e.g., Cima–Gasull–Mañosas, "Different approaches to the global periodicity problem", 2012) discuss the classification and note that no further globally periodic examples beyond the classical short list have been found, but a complete classification has not been established. No source found that resolves the question for the full family with positive coefficients.

status_evidence.title: Different approaches to the global periodicity problem
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the global periodicity problem for rational recurrences and lists the small number of known globally periodic examples without providing a full classification.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of globally periodic rational recurrences in this family remains an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Rational periodic sequences for the Lyness recurrence
status_evidence.snippet: Studies which periods are possible for Lyness-type rational recurrences, restricted to positive values yields periods 1, 5, 9.
status_evidence.claim: Even for the Lyness subfamily the periodicity question is delicate, supporting that the broader classification problem is still open.
